game: CIN@MIA Week 5 2026 (kickoff, spread, total, venue, weather not saved; morning injury report only)

script.base: No spread or total is saved, so this is a form script, not a market script. Cincinnati has been a pass-volume offense (Higgins 33 targets/342 yards and Chase 24/200 over weeks 2-4) while Miami has been a committee run offense with a runner at QB (Gordon 29/148, Achane 23/91, Willis 13/73) against a Cincinnati defense allowing 4.86 YPC. Base case is competitive and moderate pace: Miami runs enough to stay on schedule, Willis still has to throw to Washington as the only consistent target (20 targets, 166 yards), and Cincinnati throws because that is how they have moved the ball, with Brown in a 10-16 carry band rather than a 20-carry clock-kill.
script.flip1: Higgins (groin) and/or Chase (concussion) are inactive or snap-capped, both Questionable on the nflverse report. Cincinnati's pass game compresses to Meyers, Gesicki, Tinsley and Brown checkdowns, the score stays lower, and Miami can lean Gordon/Achane/Willis and lead late, which cuts Washington's routes.
script.flip2: Miami blitzes at its 29% rate and Burrow falls from +0.21 EPA/dropback unblitzed to -0.13 when blitzed, so deep Higgins/Chase shots stall and the game becomes a short-throw slog. The other explosive flip is Cincinnati scoring early, Miami abandoning the run, Gordon's carries dying and Washington/Bell targets spiking.

injury_fallout: CIN S Kyle Dugger is Out (quad) and S Bryan Cook is Questionable (ankle), so Miami's intermediate/deep answers (Washington 177 air yards, Bell 208 air yards over weeks 2-4) face a backup safety look (nflverse). CIN WR Tee Higgins (groin) and Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) are both Questionable, and WR Colbie Young (knee) is Questionable: if either star sits, Meyers (15 targets/111 yards L3), Gesicki (8/77) and Tinsley (7/49) absorb; if both play, Higgins stays the alpha (33/342/404). CIN LB Swayze Bozeman is Questionable (groin). MIA CB Reese Taylor is Out and CB Storm Duck is Questionable, which softens the perimeter for Higgins/Chase/Meyers; DE Rob Beal Jr. is Out and DT Kenneth Grant is Questionable, which softens the front for Brown; LB Jackson Woodard is Questionable, which helps TE/RB. MIA TE Justin Joly and WR Caleb Douglas are Out, so Dulcich/Kacmarek and Washington/Bell/Coleman are already the pass game, but no line-move diff is saved. MIA RB Jaylen Wright is Questionable (foot): if later inactive, Gordon and Achane split extra carries and Wright's 22.5 would void. Inactives (T-90) are not in the pack.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack. Location proxy only: MIA YPA middle 9.66 (32 att), left 7.66 (41), right 7.92 (40); CIN YPA middle 9.91 (34), left 8.09 (46), right 6.53 (58). Both bleed the middle; Cincinnati is sounder to its right.
matchup.pressure: MIA blitz rate 29% and CIN EPA/dropback is -0.13 vs blitz versus +0.21 vs no blitz, so Miami pressure suppresses Burrow's deep shots and funnels checkdowns to Brown, Meyers and Gesicki. CIN blitz rate is only 16%; MIA EPA/dropback is -0.34 vs blitz versus +0.01 vs none, so Willis is protected from his bad blitz split.
matchup.bleeds: MIA run defense is ordinary (4.01 YPC, 12 runs of 10+ in 4 games) and gives up 12 passes of 20+ for 117 yards, with the middle the soft spot. CIN run defense bleeds (4.86 YPC, 11 runs of 10+) and the pass defense allows 15 passes of 20+ for 152 yards plus 9.91 YPA in the middle, with Dugger out.
matchup.overlap: CIN's primary target is Higgins (33 targets, 404 air yards, about 12.2 aDOT). That profile does not overlap Miami's middle bleed, and the 29% blitz is a direct mismatch, on top of the groin tag, so he is not the overlap play. The cleaner overlap is Washington, Miami's target leader at about 8.9 aDOT, into Cincinnati's middle bleed and missing safeties in a game where Cincinnati rarely blitzes. Meyers (82 air yards on 15 targets, about 5.5 aDOT) is the Cincinnati piece that actually overlaps the blitz-and-middle soft spot.

form: Using weeks 2-4 sums, not season averages, with last-4 logs oldest-first so the last three match the L3 totals. Brown rush 56, 80, 61, 10 (L3 42 carries/151 yards, 3.6 YPC, trend down); rush+rec 78, 82, 69, 81, all under 93, L3 combined about 77. Higgins 59, 95, 90, 157 (L3 342) is a healthy spike, not a morning trend, because he is groin Questionable. Chase 12, 75, 98, 27 versus a 78 line, also concussion Questionable. Washington 53, 43, 56, 67 (L3 43+56+67=166 on 20 targets), last two cleared 46.5. Gordon 7, 41, 100 is a one-game 100-yard spike; median misses 42.5. Willis rush 39, 6, 56, 11 (L3 73) has a median under 32.5 but the 56 shows the ceiling. Meyers 18, 0, 29, 82 (L3 0+29+82=111), recent trend up. Gesicki's 78 is the older game; L3 is only 77 yards, so 26.5 is not a trend over. Coleman 0, 3, 3 on 118 air yards has not converted, but one explosive is the whole under. Wright -1, 11, 7 and L3 7 carries/18 yards, all far under 22.5, but he is foot Questionable and CIN allows 4.86 YPC.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both leans lost. Washington finished under 46.5 because Miami did what the run data said: Gordon, Achane and Willis carried the offense against a 4.86 YPC Cincinnati front, the game never forced seven targets, and the 43-yard game was the template, with Bell's deep air yards taking the one explosive. Meyers finished under 24.5 because the zero in weeks 2-4 was the role, not the 82, once Miami spent its 29% blitz taking away the underneath and the stars, if active, soaked the targets again. The missing Meyers price may also have been a bad number we could not see. The Higgins 'lock' that was passed would have been the other Monday loss if he was on a groin snap count.
slip_story: One competitive-game story, not a shootout stack and not a clock-kill stack: week-5 pass roles hold. Washington over is the Miami WR1 leg into a safety-depleted, low-blitz Cincinnati defense. Meyers over is the Cincinnati short/intermediate leg into a blitzing, middle-soft Miami defense, and it does not need Higgins or Chase to sit. They win together if the game stays competitive and both QBs throw at a normal rate. They lose together in the slog flip (Miami run control plus a Burrow-blitz stall). They split if Miami blows Cincinnati out. Do not add a total, a TD, Higgins, Chase, or Gordon until inactives. No bet placed.
